messages:
Carla Nguyen: Quick sync — we need a decision on the "gatekeeper" approach for private deploy launch. Field teams want a single lightweight handshake that covers: IP allowlists, tenant routing, and upgrade windows. Can we agree scope today?

Ashwin Patel: +1 to a single handshake payload. Keeps installer/user flow simple. Main question: do we include automatic migration of routing rules on upgrade or make it manual?

Maya Lopez: FieldOps prefers automatic but only if we can guarantee rollback without IP churn. Most customers don’t want manual cutovers.

Tom Baker: Technical constraint: automatic routing changes require us to own a short-lived maintenance window and a preflight check. We can do: preflight -> dry-run (checks only) -> apply. If apply fails, auto rollback.

Priya Rao: For enterprise customers, legal/security will want an explicit opt-in for automatic changes. We should default to "manual" but make automatic available for contracts that opt in.

Ashwin Patel: Proposal: default manual, opt-in automatic. Define two modes in handshake config: "apply_mode": "manual|auto". Also include "maintenance_window" optional timestamp and "dry_run": true/false.

Carla Nguyen: Sounds reasonable. Quick draft of handshake schema to review:

```json
{
  "customer_id": "string",
  "tenant_id": "string",
  "ip_allowlist": ["cidr"],
  "routing_preference": "region|edge|customer-managed",
  "apply_mode": "manual|auto",
  "maintenance_window": "RFC3339 timestamp (optional)",
  "dry_run": true/false,
  "rollback_on_failure": true
}
```

Maya Lopez: Add a "contact_on_failure" field — we need paging info so on-call is alerted immediately if auto apply fails. Also add "upgrade_policy": "canary|all-at-once|staged".

Tom Baker: Agree. Also add a "kv_cache_version" or "runtime_hint" so upgrades can validate model/runtime compatibility before touching routing.

Priya Rao: For SLAs we need to define acceptable maintenance window durations and an SLA template. Field asks: <2h for critical infra changes, prefer <30m for quick routing flips.

Ashwin Patel: Implementation notes: we'll support the handshake in the installer (on-prem) and via the private control plane (VPC). For on-prem offline installs, the handshake will be an offline JSON uploaded to the admin UI. For VPC, it's an API call.

Carla Nguyen: Action items:
- Ashwin: write handshake API and schema PR by EOD Fri (owner)
- Tom: design preflight/dry-run sequence + rollback plan by Tue
- Maya/Priya: draft field comms + SLA template by Wed
- Carla: update roadmap doc to mark default/manual + opt-in auto and list migration constraints

Priya Rao: One more: we should create a short customer-facing checklist for upgrades so NetOps knows what to expect. I can draft with Maya.

deploy-bot: New ticket created: #PD-4821 "Handshake schema + apply modes" assigned to Ashwin Patel, due 1713420000.

Ashwin Patel: Quick question — should we allow partial routing changes (subset of tenants) in a single apply? That would support staged rollouts.

Maya Lopez: Yes, allow specifying a tenant list and an "upgrade_policy": "percentage" with percent steps. Keep defaults conservative.

Tom Baker: I'll ensure runtime supports staged KV cache priming. If we do percentage-based rollouts, we need a deterministic tenant selection algorithm (hash-based) to avoid flapping.

Carla Nguyen: Good point. Let's add deterministic selection to the schema docs. If no objections, we lock scope to: handshake schema + default manual apply + opt-in auto + staged rollouts + SLA template. We'll reconvene Tue for preflight design review. :thumbsup:

Priya Rao: +1. I'll set up a 30m review on Tue and invite Security and Field success.

Ashwin Patel: On it — will push initial PR today and link here.

Maya Lopez: Thanks — this should make customer upgrades much smoother.
